rl1.name: Reinforcement learning
rl1.description: Training agents to act by rewarding good decisions and penalising bad ones, learning from trial and error.

rl1.name: Agent
rl1.description: The entity that acts inside an environment to reach a goal — on this page it acts at random, perceiving nothing and learning nothing yet.

rl1.name: Random walk
rl1.description: A path built from successive random steps — the agent's paddle moves up, stays, or down at random, the zero-baseline before any learning.

rl2.name: State space
rl2.description: The set of every situation an agent can tell apart. The grid on the court draws two of its five dimensions — where the ball is; direction, speed and paddle position stay invisible.

rl2.name: Discretization
rl2.description: Turning continuous values into a finite set of bins. For the agent the ball has no exact coordinate — only a cell, which is why the highlight jumps rather than glides.

rl2.name: Curse of dimensionality
rl2.description: Each added dimension multiplies the states to be visited, so every one is seen more rarely. This is why the finest grid is not the best: 12,000 states learn no better than 4,000, and less reliably.

rl2.name: Markov decision process
rl2.description: The formal frame behind this page: states, actions, rewards, and the assumption that the present state alone decides what can happen next.
